newsitem.title: USA: Independence Hall closed during "future" summit.
newsitem.headline: Independence Hall closed during "future" summit.

text.p: Clearing traces of asbestos from Independence Hall will take longer than expected because of the structure's age, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Tuesday.
Martha Aikens, superintendent of Independence National Park, told the newspaper that the removal of asbestos dust, which can cause cancer, from the historic brick structure will take until June.

The building will not be open to visitors during the President's Summit on America's Future, scheduled to start April 27. No events have been planned for inside the building. Other parts of the complex of buildings in Independence Park have been reopened.
The Founding Fathers met in Independence Hall, which was built in 1734, to draft the Declaration of Independence and then two decades later the Constitution.
The building will be shrouded in plastic sheeting until technicians have removed traces of asbestos discovered in testing early this month.

Asbestos dust was found in the basement of a neighbouring structure called Congress Hall, built in 1789 to house the city courts but used by both houses of the new national legislature between 1790 and 1800.

About 2,500 tourists visit the Independence Hall complex daily, said National Park Service officials. They said it was unlikely that earlier tourists had been exposed to the small amounts of dust found.
